question.problem:
Consider the matrix $B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3$ are the eigenvalues of $B$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 10\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=B,$ where $D$ is a diagonal  matrix.

current_example.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are $\lambda_1={\color{blue}4}$ and $\lambda_2={\color{red}3},$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14152180/assets/9feff06a6d717e5f56fbfedcec44ebb57d4240192202fda3f3537a36d222f5ee.svg)

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_1={\color{blue}4},$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_2={\color{red}3}.$

Therefore, we get
